steps.title: Import Vue and create the main component
steps.instruction: Import Vue and create a functional component named App with a basic template structure that returns a div element.
steps.hint: In Vue, you can create a component using a function that returns a template. Start by importing Vue and defining your component.
steps.seedCode: // Import Vue and create the App component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You will have imported Vue and created the main App component with a basic template structure.
successCriteria: Vue is imported from 'vue' and a functional component named App is created that returns a template with a div element.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported Vue and created the App component with the correct structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you've imported Vue and created a component named App that returns a template with a div.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to import Vue and create a functional component named App that returns a template with a div element.

steps.title: Initialize a reactive style object
steps.instruction: Inside the App component, add a data property that returns an object containing style properties. For example, create a property called 'boxStyle' with initial values like width, height, and backgroundColor.
steps.hint: In Vue, reactive data is defined inside the data option as a function that returns an object. Each property in that object becomes reactive.
steps.expectedOutcome: The App component now has a reactive data property containing style values that can be used for inline styling.
successCriteria: The data function returns an object with at least one property (e.g., boxStyle) that itself is an object containing style properties like width, height, or backgroundColor.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a reactive style object. This object will allow us to apply dynamic inline styles to elements in the template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added the data function, but make sure it returns an object with a style property (like boxStyle) that contains CSS properties as key-value pairs.
steps.feedbackWrong: The data function should return an object containing your style properties. Try adding something like: boxStyle: { width: '100px', height: '100px', backgroundColor: 'lightblue' }

steps.title: Add a div with inline style binding
steps.instruction: Inside the template, add a div element and bind its style attribute to the styleObject using v-bind:style.
steps.hint: Use v-bind:style to apply the reactive style object to an element's inline styles.
steps.analogousExample:
// Binding a style object to a div
Styled content
steps.expectedOutcome: A div element with inline styles bound to the reactive styleObject will appear in the template.
successCriteria: The template contains a div element with v-bind:style="styleObject" attribute.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully bound the style object to a div element using v-bind:style.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a div, but make sure to bind its style attribute to styleObject using v-bind:style.
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding a div element with inline style binding. Check that you've used v-bind:style="styleObject" on the div.

steps.title: Add static inline styles to an element
steps.instruction: Add another div element below the existing styled div, and apply static inline styles directly in the template using the v-bind:style directive with a literal object.
steps.hint: You can write the style object directly in the template like v-bind:style="{ color: 'red', fontSize: '24px' }". Place this new div after the existing one.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: static inline style in Vue template
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will contain two styled divs: one using the reactive styleObject and another using static inline styles.
successCriteria: A second div element with v-bind:style directive containing a literal style object is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added static inline styles directly in the template. This shows how you can apply styles without defining them in the data object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a new element, but check that it has the v-bind:style directive with a literal style object (like { color: 'red', fontSize: '24px' }).
steps.feedbackWrong: The step requires adding a new div with static inline styles using v-bind:style. Make sure you add the element and include the style directive with a literal object.

steps.title: Create a method to update styles
steps.instruction: Inside the component's methods object, add a method named updateStyle that changes the styleObject's color property to 'red'.
steps.hint: Add a methods property to the component configuration, then define a function inside it.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a method that can modify the styleObject when called.
successCriteria: A method named updateStyle is defined in the methods object, and it sets styleObject.color to 'red'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created a method that updates the style object.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added a methods object with an updateStyle method that changes the color property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method wasn't added correctly. Check that you've defined a methods object with an updateStyle function inside.

steps.title: Add a button to trigger style changes
steps.instruction: Add a button element inside the template, below the styled div, with the text 'Change Style' and wire its click event to call the style update method you'll create next.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with @click directive to call a method. You'll define the method in the next step.
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with click handler
<button @click="updateStyle">Change Style</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled 'Change Style' appears below the styled div, ready to trigger style updates when clicked.
successCriteria: A button element with text 'Change Style' and @click directive is added to the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added a button that will trigger style changes. Next, you'll define the method it calls.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but make sure it has the text 'Change Style' and uses @click to call a method.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button is missing or not correctly set up. Add a <button> with @click and the correct text.

steps.title: Add conditional inline styles
steps.instruction:
Add a paragraph element (

) with inline styles that change based on a condition. Use a ternary operator in the style binding to apply different background colors depending on a boolean value.
steps.hint: You can add a new data property like 'isActive' and bind it to the style attribute with a ternary expression.
steps.analogousExample:
// Conditional style binding example

Conditional paragraph
steps.expectedOutcome: A paragraph element with conditional inline styles appears in the template, and the styles change based on a condition.
successCriteria: The template contains a paragraph element with a style binding that uses a ternary operator to conditionally apply different background colors.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional inline styles using a ternary operator in the style binding.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but the style binding might not be using a ternary operator for conditional styling. Try using :style="{ backgroundColor: condition ? 'color1' : 'color2' }".
steps.feedbackWrong:
The paragraph element with conditional inline styles is missing or incorrect. Make sure to add a

tag with a style binding that changes based on a condition.

steps.title: Create a toggle for conditional styling
steps.instruction: Add a boolean data property called 'isToggled' and initialize it to false in the data() function.
steps.hint: In the data() function, add a new property 'isToggled' with the value false.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a reactive boolean property 'isToggled' that can be used to control conditional styling.
successCriteria: The data() function returns an object containing 'isToggled' property set to false.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the toggle state. This boolean will control conditional styling in the next steps.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've added 'isToggled' as a property in the data() return object with the value false.
steps.feedbackWrong: The toggle state wasn't added correctly. Check that you've added 'isToggled' to the data() return object with the value false.

steps.title: Add computed property for dynamic styles
steps.instruction: Add a computed property named 'dynamicStyle' that returns a style object with a background color based on a reactive data property.
steps.hint: Use the computed option in your Vue component to create a property that returns an object with CSS properties.
steps.expectedOutcome: A computed property named 'dynamicStyle' is added to the component, which returns a style object with a backgroundColor property.
successCriteria: The component has a computed property named 'dynamicStyle' that returns an object with at least a backgroundColor property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a computed property for dynamic styles. This allows you to create complex style logic that automatically updates when reactive data changes.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a computed property, but make sure it's named 'dynamicStyle' and returns an object with a backgroundColor property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The computed property wasn't added correctly. Remember to add a computed property named 'dynamicStyle' that returns a style object.

steps.title: Apply computed styles to an element
steps.instruction: Add a new div element below the existing styled div and bind its style attribute to the computed style property.
steps.hint: Use v-bind:style or :style to bind the computed property to the div's style attribute.
steps.analogousExample:
// Binding a computed property to style
Dynamic content
steps.expectedOutcome: A second div element appears with styles determined by the computed property.
successCriteria: A new div element is added with style binding to the computed property.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully applied computed styles to an element, completing the inline styles lesson.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a div, but make sure it's bound to the computed property using :style or v-bind:style.
steps.feedbackWrong: The new div element with computed style binding is missing. Add a div and bind its style to the computed property.
